title: 1 Kings 12 through 2 Kings 20 and the relevant prophetic books — biblical text and canonical geography
license: CC0 / public domain according to project research supplied 2026-08-29
verifiedAt: 2026-08-29 — licensing status supplied by user research; official-source release check still recommended
notes: Primary source for biblical narrative sequence and place-names. The text does not by itself establish modern coordinates, archaeological correlations, or year-exact political borders.

title: Batch 5 Divided Kingdom + Prophets Curation Methodology
notes: Separates canonical narrative, archaeological site identification, historical chronology, extra-biblical inscriptions, political reconstruction, and route inference. Exact Assyrian campaign dates are distinguished from approximate prophetic settings.
verificationNote: Project-authored curation methodology; no external source verification claim is implied.

title: A History of Ancient Israel and Judah
author: J. Maxwell Miller and John H. Hayes
notes: Historical synthesis used for the divided-monarchy framework. Political reconstruction remains subject to debate and is not converted into surveyed borders.

title: Anchor Bible commentaries on 1–2 Kings
author: Mordechai Cogan; Mordechai Cogan and Hayim Tadmor
notes: Used for royal chronology, Assyrian context, textual geography, and historical interpretation of Kings. Exact edition/page pinpointing remains a later editorial task.

title: The Context of Scripture
author: William W. Hallo and K. Lawson Younger Jr., eds.
notes: Translation/reference corpus for ancient Near Eastern inscriptions. Used as a gateway to royal inscriptions rather than treating royal propaganda as neutral reportage.

title: Neo-Assyrian royal inscriptions relevant to Israel and Judah
organization: Primary inscriptions; cross-checked through standard scholarly translations
notes: Includes Shalmaneser III (Qarqar/Kurkh and Black Obelisk), Tiglath-pileser III, Sargon II, and Sennacherib. Royal numbers, victory claims, and ideological rhetoric are interpreted critically.

title: Mesha Stele / Moabite Stone
notes: Dhiban inscription of King Mesha describing Moabite conflict with Israel/Omri. It overlaps the geopolitical world of 2 Kings 3 but does not simply duplicate the biblical campaign narrative.
dateLabel: Ninth century BCE; commonly placed in the mid-ninth century

title: Tel Dan Aramaic Stele
notes: Fragmentary victory inscription from Tel Dan. The reading “House of David” is widely accepted; attribution of the stele to a specific Aramean ruler remains debated.

title: Kurkh Monolith of Shalmaneser III — Qarqar campaign inscription
notes: Records the battle of Qarqar and names Ahab of Israel in the anti-Assyrian coalition. Troop totals are royal-inscription claims, not treated as independently verified census figures.

title: Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III
notes: Includes a scene and caption conventionally understood as tribute from Jehu of Israel, using the Assyrian dynastic label “house/son of Omri.” The monument postdates the depicted tribute event.
dateLabel: Monument: ninth century BCE; Jehu tribute episode conventionally c. 841 BCE

title: Sargon II inscriptions concerning Samaria
notes: Sargon II claims conquest/deportation connected with Samaria. Their relationship to Shalmaneser V’s siege and the biblical chronology is treated as a historical problem rather than a single certain narrative.

title: Sennacherib’s 701 BCE campaign inscriptions and Lachish reliefs
organization: Neo-Assyrian royal inscriptions and palace reliefs
notes: Assyrian sources describe the campaign against Judah, the capture of Lachish, and Hezekiah confined in Jerusalem “like a bird in a cage,” but do not claim the capture of Jerusalem.

title: Siloam Tunnel Inscription
organization: Iron Age Hebrew inscription from Jerusalem
notes: Describes the meeting of two tunneling teams. The inscription itself does not name Hezekiah; its association with Hezekiah’s waterworks depends on archaeological and biblical context.
dateLabel: Late Iron Age II; commonly late eighth to early seventh century BCE context

title: The Renewed Archaeological Excavations at Lachish (1973–1994)
author: David Ussishkin
organization: Institute of Archaeology, Tel Aviv University
notes: Major excavation publication for Iron Age Lachish and the Assyrian destruction/siege context.

title: Samaria-Sebaste excavations and Iron Age capital studies
notes: Used conservatively for the securely identified capital site, palace/administrative remains, ivories, and later phases. Individual finds are not assigned to named biblical persons unless warranted.

title: Archaeology and history of the Northern Kingdom of Israel
notes: Used to balance textual geography with settlement, monumental architecture, and changing chronological models for Tirzah, Samaria, Jezreel, Hazor, Megiddo, and related sites.

title: Shoshenq I Bubastite Portal / Karnak Levantine campaign list
dateLabel: Shoshenq I; Levantine campaign commonly dated c. 925 BCE
notes: Independent Egyptian evidence for a Levantine campaign. The surviving place list and relief program are not treated as a line-by-line parallel to 1 Kings 14 or 2 Chronicles 12.
